correctness.rationale: Exact Taylor remainder identity (1) retains a strictly positive cosine curvature integral at h=2/Lambda. SPD Rayleigh inequality ensures other terms nonnegative, compactness and vanishing steps force convergence to a single binary point. Congruence/inertia yields an unstable eigenvalue at every competing binary equilibrium; real-analytic Jacobian nontriviality at the all-zero equilibrium yields Luzin N-inverse. The noninvertible local center-stable theorem (Muşat--Boumal Theorem 5) then establishes all necessary null basins, including the supercritical phase-opposition equilibrium. Checked scalar and two-dimensional boundaries, no wrapped-fixed-point claim at supercritical steps. The standalone checker tests finite identities but is not the proof.

originality.rationale: The primary 2026 source establishes strict cosine Lyapunov decrease only below 2/Lambda, and an almost-everywhere phase-opposition basin only below 1/Lambda. The present positive integral remainder rigorously closes equality and combines the resulting all-orbit convergence with noninvertible CSMT/null-preimage basin avoidance, yielding the exact inclusive global-attraction threshold and supercritical Haar-null basin. Closest general saddle-avoidance theorems are credited and do not imply endpoint strictness. Relevant own-claim and published-finding corpus comparisons address injectivity, supercritical cycles, or unrelated critical relaxation; no demonstrated stronger implication. Residual possibility of undiscovered subsumption remains.
